findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — the light-theme value was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` inside the new `dark-light-choose(...)`, so light themes render this bold link much lighter (low contrast) and the dark branch uses 30% instead of the 70% complement; the two arguments appear swapped and it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent `.title` (50%) and eliminating the name/title visual hierarchy in light themes; the first argument should stay 30% (with a 70% dark complement)

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 — same `.name` regression on mobile: light value changed from 30% to 50%, now indistinguishable from the adjacent `.title`; should be (30%, 70%)

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:101 — `.custom-message-length` light value was flipped from 70% to 30% (and the dark branch from 30% to 70%), while the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:91) correctly keeps (70%, 30%); mobile light themes now get much darker text than before and mobile/desktop disagree in both branches; should be (70%, 30%) to match desktop

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — the `h3` light value changed from 20% to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent `h4` and inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss:318 keeps 20%); should be (20%, 80%)

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:175 — `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` is unchanged in this diff but sits inside the same rule block being edited and has exactly the dark-theme defect this PR is fixing around it: in dark schemes `$primary` is light, so `darken()` yields mid-gray composer input text; it needs the same `dark-light-choose` treatment for the fix in this block to be complete

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

This is a verifiable visual regression introduced by the diff and also inconsistent with `common/base/user.scss` where `.name` remains 30% (with a 70% dark complement).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which uses `30%` for the first branch and `70%` for the second. In the same PR, the desktop counterpart (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`) sets `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`, matching the common pattern throughout the diff. This makes mobile inconsistent with desktop and appears to invert/lighten/darken intent for the branches.

The desktop counterpart (`desktop/topic-post.scss` around the `a.star h3` block) uses `dark-light-choose(...20%..., ...80%...)`, so the mobile change is an inconsistent and likely unintended visual regression introduced by this diff.
